circuits.title: Three connections that operate the active grille shutters
circuits.scope: 2.3L engine, with active grille shutters fitted.
circuits.summary: The active grille shutters are movable blades behind the front grille. Their motor opens or closes the blades to balance cooling airflow, warm-up and aerodynamic drag. This drawing shows the three electrical paths that make that happen: operating power, a ground return, and a two-way communication wire to the engine controller.

components.label: Active grille shutter actuator
components.role: A small control unit and motor are built into the actuator. The control unit receives a requested position and drives the motor; the linked shutter blades move together. C1651 joins this assembly to the vehicle wiring.

components.label: Powertrain control module (PCM)
components.role: The engine controller decides how far to open the shutters using operating information such as vehicle speed, coolant temperature and air-conditioning pressure. Its LIN connection also receives position and fault information from the actuator.

components.label: Fuse F42 and the power feed
components.role: The supply originates at the 15 A F42 fuse in the battery junction box on drawing 33-1. Splice S112 branches that supply to continuation A and this shutter circuit. The feed is labeled hot in Start or Run.

components.label: Ground G104 through splice S128
components.role: The actuator ground joins the GD120 circuit at splice S128 and reaches ground point G104. The black/green conductor provides the actuator ground path; it is separate from the LIN communication circuit.

circuits.label: Operating power
circuits.explanation: The gray CBK03 wire brings the Start/Run supply from continuation A to the actuator. It supplies operating energy; it does not carry the requested shutter position.

circuits.label: LIN command and feedback
circuits.explanation: LIN means Local Interconnect Network. This single communication conductor links the PCM to the actuator: the PCM sends position requests, and the actuator returns position and fault information. It is not a simple on/off motor power wire.

circuits.label: Actuator ground

terminals.function: Actuator ground through S128 to G104

circuits.explanation: The black/green GD120 wire connects the actuator ground terminal to the grounded network shown at G104. The dot labeled S128 marks the splice joining these conductors.

connections.description: Power reaches the actuator through the matching continuation A on this page. F42 protects this supply circuit; the gray wire carries its operating power to the actuator.
A two-way LIN communication link carries the requested position and the returned position/fault information.
The drawing connects the actuator ground through the labeled splice to the ground point.

continuations.title: Cooling Fan — diagram 1
continuations.description: Follow continuation A to the F42 15 A supply and splice S112. The fan-motor circuits on that sheet are separate from this shutter motor.

continuations.title: Electronic Engine Controls — 2.3L
continuations.description: Find the PCM connection at C1551B cavity 50. The reference identifies the related controller drawing.

continuations.title: Grounds — diagram 3
continuations.description: See the wider GD120 ground network, splice S128 and ground G104.

continuations.title: Front component locations
continuations.description: Locate the active grille shutter connector C1651 and the relevant ground/splice area. This is a location map, not another electrical connection.

readingGuide: The three cavity numbers belong to C1651: 3 is power, 2 is LIN, and 1 is ground. C1651 has a fourth cavity in its connector view, but that cavity is unassigned here.
Follow the circuit ID as well as the color. CBK03, VDN06 and GD120 identify different electrical jobs even though they enter the same actuator.
The letter A is a continuation marker, not a terminal number. Match it to A on 33-1 to follow the power feed across the page boundary.
After an engine start, the shutters can open and close to learn their end positions. That calibration movement is described as normal operation; a momentary movement alone does not establish a fault.
This is the 2.3L active-grille-shutter circuit. It does not show the fan motor being powered through the shutter actuator.
